messages:
maya: @devraj @samir getting a customer escalation from acme-inc — they're seeing intermittent 502/504s hitting /v1/embeddings during large batch uploads (batch_size=512). They say it started ~45m ago after a client release. Trace IDs: trace=acme-9f3a... , request_id=rid-7b2a. Repro steps attached below. :eyes:

maya: example client curl they used:
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @large-batch.json
```

maya: headers we see server-side for a failing request:
```
:method: POST
:scheme: https
:authority: api.redwood.ai
content-type: application/json
content-length: 5242880
connection: keep-alive
x-tenant-id: acme-inc
```

maya: envoy logs (edge) for the failures show repeated upstream resets and 504s:
```
[envoy] [warning] HTTP/1.1 upstream reset: connection reset by peer, downstream_rq_503:0 upstream_rq_5xx:12 upstream_rq_timeouts:4 trace=acme-9f3a...
[nginx] 504 Gateway Timeout while proxying to http://upstream-billing:8080
```

devraj: thx — first-pass thoughts: large content-length + persistent keepalive + client chunking behavior can cause upstream connection churn. Also seeing billing-service timeouts in nginx logs suggests fanout to billing for tenant quota checks is blocking. Did acme use our hosted API or Dedicated?

maya: hosted API (customer on free tier, no dedicated). Billing service shows 200ms normally but spiking to 3s for some requests at the same time window.

samir: two likely simultaneous problems: 1) keepalive pool exhaustion at the edge under big concurrent batches (envoy upstream connection pool exhausted -> reset), 2) synchronous billing check call that sometimes blocks and triggers proxy timeouts.

samir: quick mitigations to try now: reduce default keepalive_timeout/idle settings on the edge, add short-circuit fallback for billing check (return cached decision for short TTL), and ask customer to reduce batch size to 64 while we triage. Also enable per-tenant circuit breaker for acme-inc.

jess: I can push a small config tweak to the host NGINX to lower proxy_read_timeout from 30s to 10s for the biller route and enable proxy_buffering off for /v1/embeddings to avoid buffering large bodies, if infra ok with that.

ops-bot: @oncall paged dev-sre (rotation: devraj) — severity: S2, affected tenant: acme-inc, error classes: 502/504 spikes, started: 1745610000 UTC, current rate: ~3 rps failing.

devraj: assigning to myself and samir. Immediate actions I'll take:
- Collect full tcpdump from edge for 1745612300-1745612500 to confirm RSTs / FIN patterns.
- Check upstream keepalive_pool utilization graph (envoy metrics: upstream_cx_active, upstream_cx_total).
- Query billing svc traces for acme tenant during window (span ids matching trace=acme-9f3a...).

samir: I'll prepare a short client-safe guideline to send to acme: reduce batch_size, add exponential backoff, and enable chunked uploads with smaller chunks (<64KB). Sample suggestion:
```
python: embeddings.batch(items, batch_size=64, retries=3, backoff_sec=0.5)
```

maya: acme reported one reproduction flow where they stream 4 concurrent requests of 2.5MB each. They said their client toggles HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 depending on environment. Could that cause head-of-line blocking? :thinking_face:

samir: toggling between h1/h2 can increase connection churn if proxies don't reuse connections across protocols. Suggest forcing them to HTTP/2 (we support h2) or reduce concurrency.

devraj: triage note: edge metrics show a spike in upstream_cx_close with reason 'local_reset' correlated with failing traces. Also saw 429 bursts from auth-proxy at same time (token validation service), which may cascade into billing fanout delays.

jess: rolling out the NGINX tweak for the biller route in canary (2 hosts) now — will monitor error rate and p99 latency. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploybot: canary rollout started for nginx/biller-config to 2 hosts — build 5.3.1 — link: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/51321

maya: update from acme: after we asked them to reduce batch_size to 64 the failure rate dropped to near zero within 10 minutes. They are willing to keep that as a temporary workaround.

devraj: good signal. Next steps:
- samir to draft tenant guidance and client PR with example backoff.
- jess to watch canary and if good, roll to 50% then full.
- me to add a short-lived per-tenant connection limit for acme-inc and a cached billing decision (TTL 30s) behind a feature flag.
- follow-up postmortem if root cause confirmed (expected window: 48h).

samir: drafted guidance, pushing to docs and sending to acme support inbox.

jess: canary looks healthy after 8 minutes, error rate for biller route dropped ~70% on those hosts. Rolling to 50% now.

ops-bot: alert cleared for acme-inc at 1745612580 — failure rate back to baseline.

maya: thank you team — keeping this thread open until feature flags in place. Will escalate to postmortem after we have full traces. :wave:
